FILED SPECIFICATION DEFECTS, every issue page fetched and its body read on 2026-09-17,
each recorded as a deviation because each changes the rule:
  - SYSML21-408, open. SendNode's second alternative ends in `SendReceiverPart`, a name
    defined nowhere in either specification; SenderReceiverPart is defined two lines
    below it in the same clause. Repaired from the specification's own text.
  - SYSML21-624, open. SendNode writes `ActionUsageDeclaration?` where its own three
    sibling declarations and the Xtext write `ActionNodeUsageDeclaration?`. Those are
    different languages: the first carries no 'action' keyword. Three pinned corpus files
    write the keyword the literal reading rejects.
  - SYSML21-400, open. ControlNodePrefix prints `( isIndividual ?= 'individual )?` with
    no closing quote. Blocks every control node.
  - SYSML21-401, open. TriggerExpression prints `kind = ( 'at | 'after' )`, same defect.
    Blocks every timed accept.
Earlier, unchanged: KERML11-115 (PayloadFeature parens), KERML11-110, -108, -109, -112,
-83, -113, -179, -111, SYSML21-335, -336, -319, -366, -402, -449.

NOT FILED, recorded by hand on their units because they do not change the rule: a

DECIDED THIS SESSION, in deviations.json, beyond the four filed defects above:
  - ForVariableDeclarationMember, follow_xtext. The clause states
    `ownedRelatedElement += UsageDeclaration`, but UsageDeclaration is not an element: the
    pilot declares it a fragment (SysML.xtext:596), which contributes features to its
    caller's object rather than instantiating one, so it cannot be the target of a
    list-valued element assignment. Its three siblings in the same clause each assign an
    element-producing production, 8.2.2.6.2 states the identical shape in
    OwnedCrossFeatureMember over OwnedCrossFeature, and the string
    `ownedRelatedElement += UsageDeclaration` occurs in exactly ONE clause of all 558.
    Both readings accept identical text; the difference is whether the clause's own
    ForVariableDeclaration is reachable. No OMG issue names it; the tracker was searched.

LL WORKAROUNDS DECLINED this session, all the same shape — a '->' or '=>' syntactic
predicate hoisting an optional part into an explicit choice to steer the parser
generator: TerminateNode, SendNode, ActionBodyParameter, TargetParameter. The clause's
`( ... )? ActionBody` says the same thing without the predicate. Porting one would make
the grammar describe the pilot rather than the language.

NAMING DIFFERENCES that looked like conflicts and are not. The Xtext gives a local name
to a production the specification already has, or wraps a keyword in a one-literal enum.
Recorded in the decision prose of each unit, not as deviations, because the language is
the same: TransitionSourceMember = FeatureChainMember; EmptySourceEndMember and
MultiplicitySourceEndMember = EmptyEndMember and SourceEndMember; PerformedActionUsage =
the four State*ActionUsage forms with ActionBody factored out; Payload = PayloadFeature;
TargetParameter is a DIFFERENT decomposition, not a rename, and was declined;
ExposePrefix, TriggerFeatureKind, GuardFeatureKind, EffectFeatureKind, TransitionUsageKeyword,
SuccessionKeyword, ActionUsageKeyword and ReferencesKeyword each hold exactly the
clause's literal.

REDUNDANT, NOT WIDER. The Xtext writes `X?` where the clause writes `X` and X is already
nullable through Identification: UsageDeclaration in TransitionUsage, GuardedSuccession,
MergeNode, DecisionNode, JoinNode and ForkNode; Identification in PayloadParameter. Same
language, no deviation. This is the MultiplicityRange@kerml precedent, and it is the
single most common false alarm in this grammar.

THE ORACLE'S STATE GUARD was an absolute 400_000 Earley items, set when the grammar was
about 5% derived. With the grammar complete it rejected the two largest corpus files as
"pathologically ambiguous". Measured rather than assumed: those files need ~996k items at
~143 per token, and parse time scales LINEARLY in the input, so the grammar is not
ambiguous and the cap no longer fitted the corpus. It is now STATES_PER_TOKEN = 2_000, a
per-token budget, which is the property actually being guarded — real ambiguity grows
super-linearly and trips a per-token bound at any file size, where an absolute cap can
only ask whether the file is big. Four tests in test_earley.py pin it. NOTE for whoever
revisits this: 2_000 is deliberately generous, ~14x the measured need, and a textbook
ambiguous grammar (`S -> S S | x`) does NOT trip it at 500 tokens. It is a guard against
runaway cost, not an ambiguity detector.

DERIVATION CONVENTIONS, unchanged and now applied across all 554:
  - Terminals are {k: tok} with the specification's names, and the oracle lexer emits
    exactly those: NAME, STRING_VALUE, DECIMAL_VALUE, EXPONENTIAL_VALUE, REGULAR_COMMENT.
    Only whitespace and the two note forms are trivia. A real's `.` is its own token.
  - A cross-reference `[QualifiedName]` is a ref to QualifiedName.
  - The special lexical terminals (KerML 8.2.2.7, SysML 8.2.2.1.2) are written out as
    keyword alternatives: TYPED_BY, DEFINED_BY, SPECIALIZES, SUBSETS, REFERENCES, CROSSES,
    REDEFINES, CONJUGATES. REFERENCES is `'::>' | 'references'`.
  - An assignment in braces — `{ kind = 'trigger' }`, `{ isPortion = true }`, `isComposite ?=`
    — is abstract syntax and contributes no token.
  - A production that derives the empty string is written `{"k": "seq", "items": []}`.
  - A decision claims nothing its own pack does not show. The validator checks for that.

WHEN CITING AN OMG ISSUE: verify it. check_citations.py resolves receipts and file-ID
shapes, not issue IDs, so a fabricated number passes every check in this repository. A
search engine's summary is not verification either. Fetch the page and read the body.
The tracker IS reachable from this machine: `curl -sSL https://issues.omg.org/issues/<KEY>`
returns the rendered issue, and all four issues cited above were confirmed that way. An
agent without a web tool cannot verify one — check its citations yourself before
recording them.

THINGS A PARSER AUTHOR NEEDS, all recorded on their units:
  - Precedence and associativity are not in the grammar and cannot be; they are data in
    docs/operator-precedence.toml.
  - `*` is LiteralInfinity, a BinaryOperator, and the namespace-import wildcard. Nothing
    lexical separates them.
  - `()` is ambiguous between NullExpression and an empty ArgumentList.
  - RealValue takes `.5` and rejects `5.`.
  - Laziness is in the grammar, not the semantics: ArgumentExpression wraps its value in a
    reference where Argument does not, and BodyExpression is a FeatureReferenceExpression.
    TriggerExpression's 'when' branch takes an ArgumentExpressionMember for the same
    reason, where 'at' and 'after' take an ArgumentMember.
  - A FeatureChain has at least two segments by construction, which keeps
    FeatureChainMember's two alternatives from overlapping.
  - A transition effect ends in `( '{' ActionBodyItem* '}' )?`, never an ActionBody, because
    the transition's 'then' follows it and there is no terminator between them. A state
    subaction ends in ActionBody and may be a bare ';'.

KNOWN GAPS in what exists:
  - sv2-syntax lexes a REGULAR_COMMENT as trivia except where significant: parser.rs's
    `comments_significant` flag is on only inside a braced RelationshipBody and the
    annotation productions. Elsewhere a bare `/* ... */` is skipped and accepted without
    becoming a Comment element, because AnnotatingMember and AnnotatingElement as a
    DefinitionElement are not implemented. KerML 8.2.2.2 makes such a comment an element.
  - sv2-syntax's lexer is generated from keywords.json, the Xtext literal union, not from
    each language's reserved words. It has the defect the oracle had until this session:
    `expr at` and `step merge` lex `at` and `merge` as keywords in a .kerml file. The
    oracle's reserved_keywords() is the source to use.
  - grammar_next.py's corpus snippets are capped and filled in file order and matched
    loosely, so a pack can show no instance of its own construct, or show eight that are
    all the wrong construct. Several units this session record "no corpus evidence, and
    here is why" rather than cite a loose match. Read those notes before assuming a
    production is unexercised.
  - Trivia attachment is positional, not owned, and the convention is undecided.
  - parse_for_editor() does not exist; `sv2 parse` has no stdout product.
  - cargo-insta is not installed; a snapshot move needs manual promotion of each .snap.new
    with its reason.
  - grammar_check_unit.py writes acceptance and diagnostics onto any unit it is run on,
    pending ones included. Running it on a pending unit to look leaves a diff to clean up.
  - An adjudicator can reason from the Xtext's version of a production instead of the
    specification's. Check any premise about another production against the clause export.
  - Deriving needs the clause export: run .claude/scripts/export_wiki_clauses.py and set
    SV2_WIKI_CLAUSES=~/.sv2-derivation/bnf-clauses.json. grammar_plan.py refuses without
    it; the preflight reads the same variable and goes red without it.

pending_decisions.question: RESOLVED. regen_state.py recorded `git log --oneline -8` in the generated block and --check compared it, which has no fixed point: the commit carrying state.json cannot record its own hash, and amending only moves it. The gate was therefore red after every commit, for ever. Fixed by naming the compared measurements explicitly — COMPARED = (coverage, tests, pins) — and a pure is_stale() over them, with four tests including the one that says a new commit is not staleness. `commits` is still measured and written for whoever reads the block at session start; it is simply not evidence. Nothing else read it: not state_report.py, not the schema's required list. NOT weakened: coverage, tests and pins are still compared exactly as before, so an un-regenerated block after real work still fails.

RESOLVED: the derive-grammar six-phase pipeline. It runs, and the expression layer is being derived through it starting from KerML 8.2.5.8.1. Two pipeline defects had to be fixed first (plan enumerated the Xtext inventory; freeze check went red on the first derived unit); both are fixed and tested.

RESOLVED. A unit no longer embeds its clause: it keeps the citation and a sha256 of the clause text, and grammar_next.py joins the text from the local export at read time. The units are therefore committed, so the derived rules, decisions and evidence survive a clone and are reviewable in a diff, while no specification prose enters the repository. check_derivation_text.py holds the line on every gate. NOT resolved by this: a fresh clone still cannot re-derive or verify a clause without building the wikis from locally-held PDFs, which is the standing wiki-reproducibility limit.

log.summary: Closed the SysML grammar and froze the reference. 473 to 554 of 554 live units verified, none pending and none in conflict; frozen at sha256 0b9abe64f1f3ce2b, 554 productions, ledger entry 1. The oracle went from 155 to all 311 corpus files accepted, still catching all 37 negatives with none leaked. Four filed specification defects repaired and recorded, each issue page fetched and read: SYSML21-408 and -624 (both in SendNode's single line), -400 (ControlNodePrefix) and -401 (TriggerExpression). ForVariableDeclarationMember adjudicated, which left SysML with no unreachable production. The oracle's state guard was re-derived from a measurement: ~143 items per token scaling linearly, so the 400_000 absolute cap was mis-calibrated rather than the grammar ambiguous, and it is now a per-token budget with four tests. Also declared sv2-ast, sv2-hir and sv2-resolve as stub crates, and proposed ADR-0016 and ADR-0017.
